cards.front: Recall a key point about Going Out and Entertainment
cards.back: This topic covers key vocabulary and structures for going out and entertainment. You need to know the topic vocabulary, be able to use it in all four skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), and express opinions with reasons.

cards.front: What should you know about french exam tips — going out and entertainment?
cards.back: 1. For Going Out and Entertainment, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Going Out and Entertainment, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
to go out (e.g. Je sors avec mes amis le samedi — I go out with my friends on Saturday)
cinema (informal) (e.g. On va au ciné ce soir — We're going to the cinema tonight)
on the terrace (at a café) (e.g. On prend un café en terrasse — We have a coffee on the terrace)

cards.front: What does le Festival de Cannes mean?
cards.back: Cannes Film Festival (e.g. La Palme d'Or est décernée à Cannes — The Palme d'Or is awarded at Cannes)

cards.front: What does la Palme d'Or mean?
cards.back: Palme d'Or (top film prize) (e.g. Ce film a reçu la Palme d'Or — This film received the Palme d'Or)
cultural exception (policy) (e.g. L'exception culturelle protège le cinéma français — The cultural exception protects French cinema)

cards.front: What does la Fête de la Musique mean?
cards.back: Music Day (21 June) (e.g. La Fête de la Musique est le 21 juin — Music Day is on 21 June)

cards.front: What does une fête foraine mean?
cards.back: funfair (e.g. La fête foraine est pendant le 14 juillet — The funfair is during 14 July)

cards.front: What does le Carnaval de Québec mean?
cards.back: Québec Winter Carnival (e.g. Le Carnaval de Québec est magnifique — The Québec Carnival is magnificent)

cards.front: What does un feu d'artifice mean?
cards.back: fireworks display (e.g. Il y a un feu d'artifice ce soir — There are fireworks tonight)

cards.front: What does aller en boîte mean?
cards.back: to go clubbing (e.g. Samedi, on va en boîte — Saturday, we're going clubbing)

cards.front: What does le Festival d'Avignon mean?
cards.back: Avignon Theatre Festival (e.g. Le Festival d'Avignon est le plus grand festival de théâtre — The Avignon Festival is the largest theatre festival)

Students often forget to use the perfect tense for completed past activities. Wrong: Hier, je joue au foot. Correct: Hier, j'ai joué au foot (perfect tense for completed past actions). Students also mix up à and en with countries. Wrong: Je vais à France. Correct: Je vais en France (en with feminine countries starting with consonant).
